message.content: Handlers return a `{mode: ..., data: ...}` reply hash instead of a bare status string because it decouples the control flow signal from the payload, enabling the protocol engine to route responses polymorphically without branching on string literals. A bare status like `"ok"` or `"error"` forces the caller to re-parse or switch on string values, whereas a structured hash lets the framework dispatch on `mode` (e.g., `"success"`, `"timeout"`, `"retry"`) while injecting `data` directly into the response envelope. This pattern also future-proofs the API: you can add new response modes or attach metadata to `data` without changing the caller’s control logic, and it prevents the fragile “magic string” coupling that accumulates when every handler must agree on an exact status enum.
